title: Coldstart KV cache + async batching trace notes
content:
Purpose:
Investigate recurring p95/p99 spikes observed in end-to-end traces during coldstart windows for the Gen-IA model family. Hypothesis: interaction between async batching, KV cache prefetch behavior, and model-init lazy weight loading is creating unfavorable serialization points that inflate p95/p99 despite acceptable p50.

Quick summary of findings (high level):
- Observed p50 ~ 85ms, p95 ~ 410ms, p99 ~ 980ms for a representative synthetic workload (seq_len=128, simple prompt).
- Majority of extra tail time is concentrated in two stages during cold windows: "kv-fetch-wait" and "async-batcher-serialize". Combined they add ~300-650ms in worst traces.
- There are a handful of traces where model-init (weight mmap or JIT warmup) adds +200-400ms; these are correlated with node churn (autoscaler events).
- Short-term mitigations: enable concurrent prefetch (prefetch_kv=true), and use small initial batch prewarm (batcher.warmup_requests=4) when spinning up a replica.

Representative per-stage breakdown (ms) — cold window p99 sample (trace id: trace-20260308-17-9934):
- http-routing: 6
- auth+quota: 3
- request-parse: 2
- routing-decision: 4
- model-init: 220
- kv-prefetch (disk->mem, sync calls): 340
- async-batcher-serialize (awaiting kv + slot): 180
- decode/generation (first tokens): 85
- postprocess + serialize: 40
- network-write: 5
TOTAL: ~885ms (observed p99 for that trace)

What we profiled & how:
- Traces from the distributed trace store (x-trace) between 2026-03-05 -> 2026-03-08. Pulled representative traces around autoscaler up events.
- Captured spans instrumented by runtime: request, routing, kv-client.fetch, kv-client.prefetch, batcher.enqueue, batcher.wait-slot, model.load-weights, model.decode-step, output.serialize.
- Used flamegraph snapshots for the batcher thread and KV-worker thread during coldstart.
- Reproduced locally with a small cluster using the repro script: tools/repro/run_coldstart_profile.sh --model gen-ia --seq 128 --scale 3 --with-trace

Observed behaviors and hypotheses (detailed):
1) KV fetch blocking pattern:
- The KV client is doing a mix of sync and async fetches. For keys not in hot cache we do disk read -> deserialize on caller thread. That blocks the batcher slot and forces serial waits.
- Hypothesis: switching to true async IO with a background prefetch worker reduces time spent in kv-prefetch span and keeps the batcher moving.

2) Batcher serialization due to slot hold:
- When a request enters batcher and waits for KV result, the slot remains reserved; other requests can't use that slot, increasing queue time and amplifying tail latency.
- Hypothesis: release slot on 'await KV' and re-enqueue when KV completes to allow other requests to fill the batch. Need to measure overhead of dequeue/re-enqueue.

3) Model-init + node churn correlation:
- Autoscaler spin-ups during load spikes are producing some model-init spans (weight mmap + kernel compilation) visible in p99 traces. For warm nodes model-init cost is low.
- Suggestion: make model-init happen earlier in lifecycle (preload during startup), and leverage a warm pool for fast replacement.

Repro steps (short):
1) Spin 3-node test cluster: infra/mini-cluster --size 3 --region localtest
2) Run workload generator: tools/loadgen/run --qps 40 --concurrency 16 --seq_len 128 --model gen-ia --duration 10m --trace=on --tag=coldstart-test
3) After 2m, kill one node to force autoscaler create. Collect traces: tools/trace/query --tag=coldstart-test --min-duration 200ms > /tmp/traces.json
4) Run analysis notebook: notebooks/trace_analysis/ipynb/coldstart_kv_batcher.ipynb (local)

Quick instrumentation tweaks to try (dev decisions):
- Change kv-client.fetch to be fully async and ensure fetch span splits into queue+io+decode subspans. (Low risk.)
- Modify batcher to support "slot-release-on-kv-await" flag behind feature gate. (Medium risk: reordering semantics.)
- Add a short-lived warm pool param in autoscaler (min-ready=1) to avoid simultaneous model-init across many replicas. (Low-medium risk operationally.)

Short experiments run so far (results):
- Async KV worker (branch pr/842) reduced median kv-prefetch span from 190ms -> 28ms under test where backing store is local SSD. p95 dropped from 430ms -> 130ms.
- Batch slot release prototype reduced queue hold time but introduced a small extra enqueue overhead (~3-4ms). Combined with async kv, p99 improved from ~980ms -> ~320ms in our synthetic run.
- Warm pool (min-ready=1) eliminated model-init spikes in 93% of test traces where autoscaler replaced nodes.

Open questions and risks:
- Does releasing batcher slots break ordering/priority semantics for requests relying on FIFO? Need to audit any downstream assumptions (billing/trace attribution).
- For multi-tenant nodes, prefetching more aggressively could increase IOPS and negatively affect co-located workloads. Need to compute IO budget and default limits.
- Coldkeys in KV can be large (embedding blobs). Async decode still consumes CPU; if many concurrent prefetches run we may saturate CPU. Consider throttling.

Next steps / action items:
- Omar: open performance PR to turn on async-kv as opt-in flag and add more granular spans (due 2026-03-14). (linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842)
- Priya: run longer 4-hour soak with batcher-slot-release + async-kv on staging and collect traces + SLO impact matrix (due 2026-03-18).
- Me (Lena): update trace sampling rules to capture a higher fraction of coldstart traces for the next 2 weeks; add dashboard tile for kv-prefetch p95/p99 per-model.

Notes to self / heuristics learned:
- Tail latency for batched systems often comes from out-of-band IO (kv, external lookups) where request holds critical batching resources. Fix: either move IO off critical path or make batcher more forgiving (release slot).
- Small enqueue/dequeue overhead (~3ms) is worth it if it prevents a slot being wasted for 300+ms.

Relevant traces for followup (ids): [trace-20260308-17-9934, trace-20260307-03-2101, trace-20260306-11-4120] — full export in linked_artifacts github gist in PR 842.

If anyone wants to pair on the flamegraphs tomorrow ping on #eng-runtime and I'll share the in-session recording.
